Class DiaryEntry

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.DiaryEntry
public class DiaryEntry extends Object
Entity class representing a single diary entry in the application.

Role and Responsibility

The DiaryEntry class stores all information related to a single diary entry. It represents the core content that users create and interact with in the diary application. Each entry has a title and content, created by an author at a specific point in time, with the ability to later edit the title and content.

Information Stored and Data Type Justification
  • Title (title): The title of the diary entry, stored as a String. The data type string provides flexibility in lenght.
  • Author (author): The author who has written the entry, stored as an Author object. Using a reference to an Author object (rather than just a name string) enables linking entries to author statistics and supports future extensions. It also maintains the relationship between entries and their creators.
  • Content (content): The content of the diary entry, stored as a String. As diary content is text in a variaty of lengths, and a String can handle anything from a single sentence to lengthy entries.
  • Date (date): The timestamp of when the diary entry was created, stored as LocalDateTime. LocalDateTime provides a precice date and time.
Mutability Assessment

Both title, content, author and date is set at creation. The title and content is typed in by the user, while the author is set to the author connected to the user logged in at that moment. The time is set to the time of creation. The title and content can later be changed, but the author and date are immutable and final.

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

This class follows a permissive/accepting strategy for invalid data:

  • Null or blank values: The constructors accept any values for title, author, content, and date without validation. This allows flexibility for JSON deserialisation where fields may be reconstructed incrementally. The calling code (e.g., DiaryUserInterface) is responsible for validating user input before creating entries.
  • Null author: If a null author is passed, subsequent calls to getAuthor().getName() will throw a NullPointerException. The design assumes the calling code provides valid author references.
  • Null date: The second constructor allows a null date, which would cause issues in toString() and date-based searches. This is accepted to support flexible deserialisation with JSON.

      public DiaryEntry(String title, Author author, String content)
      Creates a new diary entry using the current date and time as the creation date.

    • DiaryEntry

      public DiaryEntry(String title, Author author, String content, LocalDateTime date)
      Creates a new diary entry with a specified date.
